origin.description: Flatten with a comma separator, and drop an Oxford comma when the vector has two pieces.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

arguments.name: last
arguments.text: A single string used before the final piece. A leading comma is removed when string has length 2.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: When TRUE, missing values are removed inside str_flatten. The length used for the Oxford comma is the length before that removal.

origin.details: The pieces are joined with ", ". If last starts with a comma and there are exactly two elements, that comma is stripped first, so two names do not gain a serial comma. Three or more names keep it.
origin.example:
cat(paste0("str_flatten_comma(letters[1:3], \", and \") returns ", str_flatten_comma(letters[1:3], ", and "), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_flatten_comma(letters[1:2], \", and \") returns ", str_flatten_comma(letters[1:2], ", and "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Flatten on ", " after a leading-comma check that calls stringi.stri_detect_regex and stringi.stri_replace_first_regex.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: last
arguments.text: None uses the comma throughout. A string that starts with a comma loses that comma when there are two pieces.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: R's na.rm, applied by str_flatten after the two-piece test.

translation.details: The two-piece test uses the original length. Removing a missing value afterwards can leave one piece, and last is then unused. The result is a list of length 1.
translation.value: A list of one string, or one NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.join import str_flatten_comma
print("str_flatten_comma(letters[1:3], \", and \") returns " + str_flatten_comma(list("abc"), ", and ")[0] + ".")
print("str_flatten_comma(letters[1:2], \", and \") returns " + str_flatten_comma(list("ab"), ", and ")[0] + ".")
